The job runner starts a job when its heavy slot fits (2 slots; a light job takes none, a heavy job of 2 threads or fewer half), the running jobs' threads plus its own fit 14, the system's idle CPU covers its threads (hand-started runs count as busy), the running jobs' reserved memory (--mem-gb, or the measured peak_gb when higher) plus this job's fits total memory minus 1 GB, and free memory is at least --mem-gb + 1 GB; --mem-gb is a reservation, so set it to the job's peak (jobs.py status shows each job's peak_gb; add warns and records mem_gb_low when --mem-gb is under the last peak of the same script and first argument). A job that can never start (threads over 14, --mem-gb + 1 over total memory, a broken file) is moved to done as refused.

A job that can never start (threads over 14, --mem-gb + 1 over total memory, a broken file) is moved to done as refused. Exception: peak_gb is the process tree's working set, mapped file pages included, so for learn.py and other readers of the memory-mapped feature cache it overstates the reservation (a 40k learn: peak_gb 5-6.6, commit about 1 GB); give such jobs --mem-gb 2.5 and ignore add's mem_gb_low warning for them: at 5.5 they could not start and held the queue's reservation.
